newsitem.title: USA: Caspian group plans first Karabakh well next year.
newsitem.headline: Caspian group plans first Karabakh well next year.

text.p: Caspian International Petroleum Co plans to drill the first exploratory well in the Caspian Sea's Karabakh prospect offshore Azerbaijan in mid-1997, Pennzoil Co said.
The well is planned for a depth of 4,200 meters in water depth of 185 meters, the company's statement said.

The plan was set at a Contractors Management Committee meeting last week which also formally approved the contract to Caspian Geophysical, an American-Azerbaijan joint venture, to perform a 3-D seismic survey of the Karabakh prospect.
The total contract for acquiring and processing the data is $7.6 million, Pennzoil said.

It said the survey is expected to start in mid-September over an area covering 626 square kilometers, which will provide effective coverage of the entire prospect where the water depth ranges from 150 to 225 meters.
During the meeting, V.A. Zazirny of NK LUKoil LKOH.RTS was elected chairman of the committee.

The committee adopted a budget of $18,393,000 for 1996 and $35,275,000 for 1997. It also said the company has opened and evaluated bids for casing and wellhead and expects to award contracts in the near future.

The minimum work program specified by the Karabakh Production Sharing Agreement includes the 3-D seismic program, drilling of at least three exploration wells during a three-year period and an environmental baseline study and site investigation, Pennzoil said.
The contractor parties to the agreement are LUKoil, 12.5 percent, Agip SpA, 5 percent, LUKAgip NV, 45 percent, Pennzoil, 30 percent, and the Azerbaijan state oil company, 7.5 percent.
